name: source-authority-mapping
description: Traces a claim, artifact, or contract through semantic ownership, source location, projections, delivery routes, receiving use, and promotion.

contract.what: A portable method for making the authority and receiving path of a claim, artifact, or contract legible across several systems.
when: Source, semantic ownership, publication, delivery, snapshotting, or downstream use could be mistaken for one another.
boundaries: The map records evidenced relations and granted decisions.
Private or gated material remains within its publication boundary.
Delivery infrastructure remains separate from semantic ownership.
contract.result: A concise lineage map that identifies the authoritative source, typed projections, current receiver, promotion boundary, and re-entry condition.

receivingUse.job: Give a cross-platform collaborator a source-to-receiver route for one material object.
receivingUse.materialResult: A repository ownership map and a reusable typed contract linked from the Context Canvas skills page.
receivingUse.completion: Another collaborator can locate meaning, current representation, projection relations, publication authority, and the receiving decision.

standing.evidenceMaturity: Observed across schema delivery, workspace reference routing, and repository ownership mapping.
standing.wakeTrigger: A cross-system promotion exposes a new authority ambiguity or unnecessary attention cost.

transferBoundary: This projection carries local instruction yield; publication rights remain with their stewards, and another system may retain its own ownership vocabulary.
